newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Astra drops on results.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Astra drops on results.

text.p: Swedish drug company Astra Ab's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) fell Tuesday, weighed by worse-than-expected earnings.
Traders in ADRs said overseas markets had been surprised by Tuesday's rebound of the Dow industrials after a drop the day before.

Astra fell 1-1/8 to 39-5/8 in volume that at midday was four times the normal daily level. The company reported Monday a one percent rise in first quarter pre-tax profit to 3.46 billion crowns, below an expected 3.93 billion crowns.
Bear Stearns analyst David Molowa cut Astra to attractive from buy. He blamed "disappointing" results for the downgrade.

British drug company SmithKline Beecham Plc rose 2-1/8 to 76 after the company announced first quarter results. The company's eight percent profit rise was at the low end of forecasts but it said underlying growth in the first quarter was excellent.

Oil stocks also largely strengthened, helped by rising crude prices and strong results from U.S. companies. Royal Dutch Petroleum Co rose 1-7/8 to 178-1/2 and British Petroleum Co was up 4-1/8 at 139.
Australian mining company Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd was among the most active ADRs. It had 2.27 million ADRs traded at midday and trade was dominated by a 2.2 million share block trade.
Further details were not immediately available.
Dutch entertainment company PolyGram NV fell 1-3/8 to 48-3/4 after reporting a drop in its first quarter profits.
Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA fell 1/2 to 110-3/8.
Advancers barely led decliners 235 to 232 among 806 ADRs. The ADR index rose 0.15 percent and volume was 41 million shares in early afternoon.
